title: Assignment 26 · Third-party rights, delegation, and assignment
summary: Third-party rights, delegation, and assignment. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Lawrence v. Fox: A creditor could enforce a promise made to his debtor for the creditor’s benefit even though the creditor supplied no consideration directly to the new promisor.

Seaver v. Ransom: A niece could enforce the husband’s promise to his dying wife to provide for the niece by will, where the wife signed her own will in exchange for that promise.

Sisney v. State: An inmate was not entitled to enforce the state’s general food-service contract because the court found no clear contractual intent to grant him an individual enforcement right.

Sisney v. Reisch: An inmate sufficiently alleged a right to enforce a settlement promising certified kosher meals to all Jewish inmates who requested them; dismissal was reversed.
